Nvidia: Scaling Quarterly Revenue Rapidly

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) primarily generates revenue by designing and selling advanced graphics processing units (GPUs), networking interconnect solutions, and accelerated computational platforms for data centers, personal computer gaming systems, enterprise professional visualization workstations, autonomous automotive applications, and cloud gaming subscription services.

It recently agreed to supply Amazon-owned AWS with additional graphics processing units and expanded its software partnership with Meta Platforms, while simultaneously introducing new hardware reference architectures intended to reduce initial infrastructure deployment time for its commercial enterprise customers.

SK Hynix: Expanding Memory Semiconductor Revenue

SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) primarily generates revenue by designing, manufacturing, and selling a wide variety of advanced memory semiconductors, including dynamic random-access memory and diverse flash memory products with specialized configurations tailored to meet application-specific customer needs across global technology markets.

It recently showcased its new tenth-generation flash memory technology and officially commenced shipments of its latest high-bandwidth memory products to customers, while separately navigating a suspended initial public offering for its United States memory subsidiary, Solidigm, and defending against an ongoing antitrust class action lawsuit.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue helps investors evaluate the total volume of products and services a company sells before deducting its operating costs, taxes, and other financial expenses. This metric reveals whether an organization is successfully attracting customers and growing its overall business volume over time.

title: Shopify vs. Amazon: Which Stock Wins When AI Agents Do the Shopping?
detail:
Shopify vs. Amazon: Which Stock Wins When AI Agents Do the Shopping?
Bobby Sankhagowit

SHOP
AMZN
META
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Shopify vs. Amazon: Which Stock Wins When AI Agents Do the Shopping? ©@William_Potter from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Shopify shares fell 8% today after its third-quarter revenue grew 32%, but its merchandise volume came in just short of Wall Street's expectations.

Shopify's checkout runs inside ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta's Muse. Amazon is building its own shopping agents and has fought to keep outside ones off its store.

Amazon trades at a much lower multiple of expected earnings, but analysts expect Shopify's earnings to grow faster through 2028: about 33% a year, against about 25% for Amazon.

Shopify looks like the better bet on agentic shopping, as long as the companies that own the agents keep using its checkout at its standard rates.

Shopify (SHOP:NASDAQ) shares fell 8% today after its third-quarter report. The timing is awkward, because Shopify has spent the year pitching itself as the checkout behind every AI shopping agent. Its president, Harley Finkelstein, said in the release that Shopify is "continuing to build commerce into every surface, every agent, and increasingly, everywhere."

Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ), up 11% this year, has a different plan: build its own agents and keep everyone else's off its store.

So if AI assistants end up doing a lot of the buying, which stock wins? Is it the platform behind millions of merchants, or the store that owns the customer?

A strong quarter that missed by a hair

Shopify's third-quarter revenue grew 32% to $3.74 billion, and operating income jumped 66% to $568 million. Free cash flow came to $816 million, a 22% margin and well above the $723 million analysts expected.

But gross merchandise volume (GMV) of $119.1 billion came in just short of the $120.1 billion analysts expected. Shopify had also beaten the top of its own revenue guidance in each of the three quarters before this one. This time, 32% growth landed inside its guide for a low-thirties rate.

For the fourth quarter, Shopify again expects revenue to grow at a low-thirties rate, a touch above the roughly 30% analysts had expected going in.

Not bad at all.

Shopify plugs into every agent

Shopify merchants already sell through ChatGPT's Instant Checkout. In January, Shopify and Google announced the Universal Commerce Protocol, which runs checkout in Gemini and Google's AI Mode. Microsoft's Copilot has Shopify's checkout built in, and Meta's Muse agent checks out with Shop Pay at Shopify's existing payments rates.

In its third-quarter 2026 investor letter, Pershing Square highlighted stocks like Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN). Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) is a technology and e-commerce company that operates online retail marketplaces, subscription services, advertising businesses, and Amazon Web Services (AWS), its cloud computing division. (NASDAQ:AMZN) stock closed at approximately $245.63 per share, with a market capitalization of about $2.66 trillion.

Pershing Square stated the following regarding Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) in its Q3 2026 investor letter:

"Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)'s share price increased 5% during the third quarter and 8% year-to-date. Business momentum remains strong across the company. AWS revenue growth accelerated to 39% in the third quarter, its fastest rate in nearly five years. The segment's backlog reached nearly $600 billion, growing at a triple-digit rate, while operating margins remained near their highest levels in history despite the ongoing buildout. The company's retail business continues to take share, with paid units growing 12%, aided by the secular tailwind of rising e-commerce penetration and the early adoption of agentic shopping.

Despite these results, Amazon remains undervalued in our view, as investors are focused on the magnitude of capital spending, with 2026 capital expenditures of approximately $220 billion and management indicating it expects to spend meaningfully more in 2027. Notably, the demand supporting this investment has become increasingly visible as management now expects AWS to grow more than 40% in each of 2027 and 2028, with a stated goal of reaching $1 trillion of annual revenue within the next five to ten years. We find the company's framework for the returns on this investment compelling, particularly as management has indicated that its payback period on AWS capital continues to shorten, and we believe the resulting growth in free cash flow is underappreciated. We believe Amazon can compound earnings at a 20%-plus rate over the long term (Click Here To Read The Letter In Detail)."

Key Takeaways

X-energy stock fell 23% in the past month as investors sold small-reactor stocks, Oklo and NuScale Power among them.

The company's own news was good: a joint development deal with American Electric Power and Amazon for a 960 MW plant in Indiana, and a finished NRC safety review of its Xe-100 reactor.

Wedbush initiated coverage at Buy with a $17 target, below the $31 consensus. That target is just under 9x forward sales, below the stock's average since its IPO.

Third-quarter results on Nov. 12 need to show X-energy has the cash to keep going until revenue from these projects arrives.

X-energy (XE:NASDAQ) stock is down 23% in the past month, and the other small-reactor stocks did even worse. Oklo (OKLO:NYSE) lost 35% and NuScale Power (SMR:NYSE) lost 31%, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 9%.

That's despite a month of real progress at X-energy, including a plant deal with American Electric Power (AEP:NASDAQ) and Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ). And on Nov. 2, Wedbush initiated coverage at Buy with a $17 target, 54% above the stock's current price.

Good news didn't save it

On Oct. 19, X-energy and AEP signed a joint development agreement for a proposed 12-unit, 960 MW Xe-100 plant near the former Breed coal plant in Sullivan County, Indiana. Amazon will help fund development and plans to buy the power. AEP says the plan aims to help Indiana without raising costs for its customers.

It's still feasibility work for now. But on Oct. 30, the NRC finished its final safety review of the Xe-100. That completes both of the main reviews the NRC needs before it can approve a construction permit.

title: Amazon's Earnings Just Hit a Record. So Why Is the Stock Down 11% From Its Peak?
detail:
Amazon's Earnings Just Hit a Record. So Why Is the Stock Down 11% From Its Peak?
Brett Schafer, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 1:12 PM EST 5 min read
AMZN
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The technology bull market is beginning to stagger just a bit. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) stock fell again after it reported earnings last week, and while it has rebounded modestly, as of midday Monday, it is still down 11% from its peak.

Earnings came in at record levels, yet investors remain nervous about the technology giant in e-commerce and cloud computing. Understanding why could help inform your decision about whether or not you should buy Amazon shares right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Robust cloud demand but a dent in cash flow

In the third quarter, Amazon's cloud division, Amazon Web Services (AWS), was the star of the show yet again. Revenue was up 39% to $46 billion, one of its fastest growth rates in years, with phenomenal earnings of $17.8 billion, resulting in a margin of 39%. Management is guiding for year-over-year revenue growth of 40% in 2027 and 2028, which would essentially double AWS' sales in just two years.

The problem is that high revenue growth at AWS will require massive up-front capital expenditures. The company's free cash flow has been negative over the last 12 months due to its $220 billion capital spending plan for 2026. It's likely to increase its capex in 2027 and 2028.

Amazon has around $100 billion in cash on its balance sheet that it could put toward funding these data center investments, but it may need to raise additional funds to fully finance its artificial intelligence (AI) build-out. The amount of long-term debt on its books stood at $173 billion as of the end of last quarter. The combination of more debt on the balance sheet and negative free cash flow will make investors more skittish about the stock.

Image source: Getty Images.
The e-commerce business is intact

The other engine of Amazon's business is commerce. Its North American commerce revenue growth decelerated to 6% year over year in Q3, which may have concerned the Street as well. In the second quarter, North American sales grew 16% year over year.

Most of the deceleration was due to a simple and obvious reason, though: Amazon moved Prime Day from Q3 last year to Q2 this year, which shifted 400 basis points (4 percentage points) of growth from Q3 to Q2 in 2026. Normalizing this switch, North American growth last quarter would have been 10%, which is quite good for a mature business generating close to $500 billion in annual revenue.

We just published the list of the 10 Best and Cheap Stocks to Buy Heading into 2027 and Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) ranks 7th on this list.

Wall Street's AI trade took a hard hit on October 30. Reuters reported that a selloff in tech shares pushed MSCI's global index down 1.5%, after results from Intel and Amazon showed how much cash AI spending is burning. Intel fell 28.6%, and the Philadelphia semiconductor index lost more than 7%, its biggest one-day drop since late June. Alphabet's shares had already slid 12.6% a day earlier, after it reported that its AI spending pushed its cash flow negative.

The nervousness had been building. Reuters reported on October 15 that South Korea's KOSPI index, home to some of the world's largest chipmakers, fell roughly 8% in a single session. Saxo Bank chief investment strategist Charu Chanana said the Asian selloff looked less like a sudden deterioration in technology fundamentals and more like a repricing of the cost of capital.

READ ALSO 10 Best Robotics Stocks to Buy That Are More Than 30% On Sale

Rates are a large part of that story. Bloomberg reported on October 4 that benchmark 10-year Treasury yields sat near 5.3%, and Franklin Templeton Institute head market strategist Chris Galipeau said the conversation would change if they reached 6%. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Robert Schiffman added that hyperscalers such as Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Oracle now have cash needs far beyond what they generate, which pushes them toward debt markets.

Western Digital made our list of the best and cheap stocks to buy for two reasons. First, its forward P/E is 9 and expected revenue growth rate for 2027 is nearly 47%. Second, it is one of the most popular stocks among hedge funds which is why WDC is one of the best cheap stocks to buy according to hedge funds.

Western Digital reported that fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 55% from a year earlier, above the range management had guided, and then pointed to something faster. It expects revenue growth of 66% to 72% in the current quarter, driven by cloud customers that now account for most of its sales and by steady demand for high-capacity drives.

Why Western Digital’s (WDC) Massive Quarter Is Only the Beginning

The profit side is improving even more quickly. Adjusted gross margin widened to 58.1%, because customers pay more per terabyte for denser drives and Western Digital is adding capacity by packing more data onto each drive instead of building more factories. Chief executive Irving Tan pointed to multi-year visibility from its largest customers. The company also expects to start volume shipments of its first heat-assisted recording drives in the first half of next year.
